note: A1+ Unit 5 Lesson 5.12, built on 2026-11-20 under the A1+ lesson standards approved 2026-10-27 and the user's 2026-11-09 rule that every A1+ lesson follows up the A1 lesson with the same number. The user asked on 2026-11-20 to "work on a1+ Unit 5 same all deal as before none stop all approved": A1+ 5.Y follows A1 5.Y with one step each, straight to Preview in batches, Gemini 2.5 Flash photos and ElevenLabs audio pre-approved, no per-lesson gates, reviewed in Preview. Five shop photos with one price card each ($45 shoes, $68 bag, $99 bike, $32 chair, $24 cake) and two grandparents behind birthday cakes with number candles (74 and 81). The age photos stay out of four-picture cards when the candles are small.

lesson.title: 5.12 Forty-five dollars
lesson.unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
lesson.goal: Say and understand prices and ages from twenty-one to ninety-nine (The shoes are forty-five dollars. / She's seventy-four.), and tell forty-five from fifty-four.
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.12 Numbers 30 to 100: A1 says the tens from thirty to one hundred; A1+ 5.12 joins a ten and a unit with a hyphen (forty-five = forty + five), the numbers kept out of A1+ since Unit 2 (house numbers stayed at twenty or round tens). Four numbers are taught as items and the others are practised with the same rule. Banks set a number against the one with its digits swapped (forty-five / fifty-four). Each photo shows one thing behind its price card, or a grandparent behind a cake with two number candles; 5.8's How much is/are …? asks and 5.11's cheaper than returns.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 5.12 thirty to ninety; A1 numbers one to nine; A1+ 5.8 How much are …? They're …; A1+ 3.5 How old …?; A1+ 5.11 cheaper than.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Stress the ten and keep the unit clear (FOR-ty FIVE); keep the -ty of forty short so it is not heard as fourteen; do not require native-like speed.
